written_by: claude-opus-5-5, one blind subagent per dataset (tests/gold/r101/rules.md and the sample only, no pass output existed), revised twice as the definition was settled for all three datasets; lead review by Claude Opus 5.5 in the session, no change

sentences.text: Core BF-1, 14 April: depth 2.1 m, pH 3.8.
sentences.note: Identifier written without 'Core' (shortest name, same form as the bare HP40 ids elsewhere); depth and pH are properties the text gives values for (In 2), the values stay in the claim.

sentences.text: Core AB-19, 10 December: depth 5.1 m, pH 3.9; the corer jammed at 5 m and was freed by J.
sentences.note: 'jammed' (fault) and 'freed' (action done to the corer) are verbs (In 3); 'J.' is a person named by initial.

sentences.text: Core AB-20, 10 December: not taken, the site was flooded.
sentences.note: 'taken' is the coring done to the core, which did not happen (In 3 + In 4); 'flooded' is the site's state; 'site' is the unnamed coring site.

sentences.text: The institute gives the Hensley Field-Work Award once a year for outstanding field work.
sentences.note: 'institute' is an organisation known only by its role, so kind; 'gives' is a light verb (the award is the thing); 'field work' kept as the activity the award is for, not an everyday act.

sentences.text: Samuel Osei was nominated, but the committee found that no entry met the standard.
sentences.note: 'nominated' is an everyday act of people (Out 8); 'entry' kept although absent (In 4); 'found' is reporting and 'met the standard' an evaluation.

sentences.text: Every project lead must submit a data management plan by 30 June 2025.
sentences.note: 'submit' is filing, an everyday act of people (Out 8).

sentences.text: Projects without a plan will not receive second-year funding.
sentences.note: 'receive' is a light verb: the funding is the thing.

sentences.text: Aiko Tanaka closed the meeting at 15:55.
sentences.note: 'closed' the meeting is an everyday act of a person, not a fault or work done to a thing (Out 8).

sentences.text: ## Field-work award
sentences.note: Heading names the one award of the section; taken as a particular although in sentence case.

sentences.text: # Seminar notice
sentences.note: The notice is the document itself (Out 5); the seminar it announces is an event.

sentences.text: Several colleagues have asked how the June conference trips are funded.
sentences.note: 'June' kept because it tells these trips apart; trips are events (In 2); 'funded' is an everyday act (Out 8); 'colleagues' is a generic people word; 'asked' is reporting.

sentences.text: Maria Lopez presented a poster on the 240 cores of the Aldmoor bog, which drew more questions than any other poster in her session.
sentences.note: 'presented' is an everyday act (Out 8); 'drew more questions' is an evaluation.

sentences.text: Maria Lopez has opened a bakery at 14 Harbour Street, in the former post office.
sentences.note: 'opened' a bakery is an act of a person, not a fault or work done to a thing (Out 8); the address is kept whole as the place named; 'former' tells the building apart.

sentences.text: # Riverton sets its 2025 works budget
sentences.note: '2025' kept because it tells this budget apart from the 2026 one; 'sets' is a light verb.

sentences.text: - Mill Lane footbridge repair: 180,000 pounds
- Harbour Street resurfacing: 95,000 pounds
- Riverside path lighting: 230,000 pounds
- Mill Lane footbridge east railing: 15,000 pounds
Councillor Priya Nandakumar welcomed the second drainage phase but asked why the resurfacing had slipped by a year.
sentences.note: Title 'Councillor' is part of how the named person is called, not a second thing; 'welcomed' and 'asked' are reporting.

sentences.text: Mill Lane footbridge: closed to all users from 3 February for repair works, for about eight weeks.
sentences.note: 'all users' is generic.

sentences.text: Harbour Street: resurfacing postponed to 2026.
The street stays open to traffic.
sentences.note: 'street' refers back to Harbour Street but is not named here, so kind; 'stays' is light and 'open' an adjective, not a verb form (Out 1, ambiguous); 'traffic' is part of 'open to traffic'.

sentences.text: The council's structural inspector, Daniel Okafor, said the culvert under Station Road is too narrow for heavy storms.
sentences.note: 'structural inspector' is Daniel Okafor in apposition: one entry per thing, kept as the name.

sentences.text: # Mill Lane footbridge reopens
The Mill Lane footbridge reopened on 28 March after eight weeks of works.
sentences.note: 'works' names the repair works here, not a generic word.

sentences.text: # Riverton Water opens its doors
sentences.note: 'opens its doors' is an idiom for an open day, not a fault or work done to a thing; 'doors' is no thing.

sentences.text: Technician Rosa Delgado showed them the station's Kestrel V-12 pump and explained how the alarms reach North Station when the site is unmanned.
sentences.note: 'Kestrel V-12' is a model name, taken as particular; 'site' is the station again (one entry per thing); 'unmanned' is an adjective; 'showed', 'explained' and 'reach' are reporting or light.

sentences.text: Children could try a hand pump in the yard, and the café sold out of cakes by noon.
sentences.note: 'sold out' is an everyday act of selling (Out 8); 'try' is light.

sentences.text: # Eastgate library back in business
sentences.note: 'back in business' is an idiom with no verb or thing.

sentences.text: The footbridge will be closed from 3 February while its railings and deck boards are renewed.
Dear Riverton Water,
In our experience a Hydra P-40 needs a new mechanical seal every 18 months of duty.
sentences.note: 'Hydra P-40' is a model name, taken as particular although the claim covers any unit; 'needs' is light.

sentences.text: Kind regards,
The station's only pump, KV12-0457, tripped three times in the first week of May on low suction pressure.
sentences.note: 'only pump' is KV12-0457 in apposition: a description, not a second name, so the id is the entry.

sentences.text: Pump HP40-2291 ran quietly.
sentences.note: 'ran' names the pump's running state; 'quietly' is manner.

sentences.text: ## Before you start
HP40-1183 ran for 6,100 hours and HP40-2291 for 2,300 hours, as HP40-1183 was kept on duty for most of the year.
sentences.note: 'ran' names the pumps' running state, one entry for both (one entry per thing); 'kept' is light, 'on duty' a state phrase.

sentences.text: Tue: Calder Pumps phoned about the seal returned from HP40-1183.
sentences.note: 'phoned' is reporting; 'returned' is the action done to the seal.

sentences.text: Tue: alarm from Harbour Station at 03:10, cleared remotely; KV12-0457 restarted on its own.
WO-318, 30 June.
